transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-06-23 16:00 UTC | Duration: 48m | Attendees: Laura (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Priya (LumaHealth Product), Mark (Security), Ellen (SRE)

Summary: quick scoping call focused on POC acceptance criteria for prompt-handling flows, how LumaHealth wants logs retained/redacted, and what benchmark traffic looks like.

00:00:01 Laura (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. Quick intros?
00:00:07 Priya (LumaHealth): Hi all, Priya Shah, head of product. We're trying to pilot patient triage messages with an LLM behind our intake flow.
00:00:15 Mark (LumaHealth): Mark Cooper, security. I'll be driving the redaction and retention side.
00:00:19 Ellen (LumaHealth): Ellen Zhao, SRE, I'll own bench runs and test infra.
00:00:25 Diego (Redwood): Diego Martinez, solutions engineering, I'll handle performance and benching.
00:00:30 Laura: Great. Goal for today: agree success criteria, get a representative traffic model, and confirm what we log vs ephemeral keep.
00:00:42 Priya: For success we care about accuracy of triage (F1-ish), 95th p99 latency under 350ms for common cases, and cost within our projected budget. Also data handling — we cannot store PHI beyond ephemeral traces.
00:00:58 Mark: Yep. SOC2 is baseline, but we have additional constraints: full audit trail for who asked what, but we can't persist raw patient identifiers. We need redaction before storage.
00:01:12 Diego: Understood. Quick clarification — when you say "can't persist raw identifiers," do you mean no plain-text PII in logs at all, or allowed if encrypted with your KMS?
00:01:22 Mark: Preferably redacted to token like <REDACTED_PATIENT_ID> in logs. If something must be stored for reconciliation, it has to be encrypted with our KMS and only accessible via a narrow service account.
00:01:34 Laura: That's doable. Redwood's Private mode supports customer KMS integrations and audit logs. For hosted pilot we can do field-level redaction before storage, or we can run ephemeral prompt streams that are not persisted.
00:01:46 Priya: For the pilot we want to test both: ephemeral stream for most flows and a redacted log for edge cases where we need human review. We want to measure how much traffic would be ephemeral vs stored.
00:02:00 Ellen: On traffic: our current intake sees roughly 12k messages/day, but only ~18% are triage flows that hit the LLM. Average prompt size is 420 tokens, response around 200 tokens. Peak concurrency is about 45 requests/sec during office hours.
00:02:18 Diego: That's a good starting point. For benching we typically synthesize a traffic model that captures token distribution: 70% fast short prompts (~120 tokens), 20% medium (400 tokens), 10% long (>1k tokens). Do those buckets map to your data?
00:02:29 Ellen: Slightly different — more medium and long. Maybe 50% medium, 35% short, 15% long. But average token lengths you listed are close.
00:02:39 Diego: OK we'll adapt. Bench plan: we'll run a 1-hour warm-up then 2 x 30-minute steady-state runs at nominal and peak (45 req/s and 65 req/s) to capture latency p50/p95/p99 and per-token cost. We'll also attach KV cache on prefix matches to mimic conversation continuity.
00:02:58 Priya: Good. Acceptance criteria — can we write them down now?
00:03:03 Laura: I'll propose a draft but let's capture live: 1) p95 latency < 350ms at nominal load, p99 < 700ms at peak; 2) quality: triage classification accuracy within 3% of baseline model; 3) redaction: zero instances of unredacted PHI in persisted logs across bench runs; 4) cost: cost per 1k tokens under X (we'll fill number after pricing).
00:03:24 Mark: For redaction verification we'll need a signed report plus a sample of logs and the regex rules used. Also want automated false-negative detection for PII in logs.
00:03:34 Diego: We can run an independent detection pass against persisted logs using your regexes plus an NLP PII tool, report false negatives. We can also demonstrate ephemeral mode where logs are not written at all.
00:03:45 Priya: Timeline? We're hoping for a two-week pilot with benching in week 1 and run-of-site integration in week 2.
00:03:53 Laura: That's consistent with our standard pilot cadence. Proposed immediate steps: exchange redaction patterns, provision a test key, upload bench harness, run bench, review results, then sign off on acceptance criteria to move to sizing.
00:04:07 Ellen: For test key we prefer a VPC endpoint so traffic stays in our cloud. Is that possible for pilot?
00:04:12 Diego: Yes — we offer a private endpoint option for pilots. We'll need a CIDR and some outbound rules. For hosted pilots we can provide a VPN or VPC peering depending on your cloud.
00:04:22 Mark: KMS — we use Azure Key Vault. Requirements: envelope encryption where Redwood can call our KMS for decryption only under governance. We need logs to show those calls.
00:04:33 Laura: Redwood supports customer-managed keys (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault). For hosted we can integrate with your vault and store tokens encrypted; access is restricted. We'll include the KMS integration checklist in the follow-up.
00:04:45 Priya: Bench metrics: we want p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, cost per 1k tokens, cache hit rate, and CPU/GPU utilization on the Redwood runtime if possible.
00:04:56 Diego: We can stream runtime metrics and provide per-request token accounting. GPU metrics can be shared at a coarse granularity due to multi-tenancy on hosted, but for Dedicated we can provide per-instance metrics. For pilot we'll provide aggregated GPU utilization and per-model throughput.
00:05:11 Mark: Also need audit logs for who queried what and policy for retention. Our compliance says logs older than 30 days must be redacted or moved to encrypted cold storage. Can Redwood set per-route retention rules?
00:05:22 Laura: Yes, Redwood Console supports per-route retention and auto-redaction policies. We'll show the retention matrix in the security docs. For pilot we can set 7-day ephemeral for most routes and 30-day encrypted for review routes.
00:05:34 Priya: One risk: prompt leakage through cached prefixes. If a conversation is cached, could the cache contain PII?
00:05:41 Diego: Good point. We treat caching as KV or prefix cache. We can apply redaction before KV is stored or store caches in encrypted form and scrub certain keys. For your use-case we recommend redacting or hashing patient identifiers prior to caching. We'll provide a config option to prevent long-term storage of raw prompt prefixes.
00:06:01 Ellen: For our bench harness we'll include synthetic PII to test redaction effectiveness. Expect us to send sample payloads with seeded PHI.
00:06:08 Mark: We'll also want a step to validate end-to-end that any persistent logs have no raw SSNs, patient names, or email addresses.
00:06:15 Diego: We'll build a small validator script that runs post-bench and outputs counts of any matches. If >0 we'll flag a failure of the redaction acceptance criterion.
00:06:24 Priya: On success criteria we also want a human review window — if the model triages incorrectly more than X times in a day we want fallback to human triage. Is that in scope for the pilot?
00:06:34 Laura: Yes, can be part of the acceptance matrix as a quality threshold and fallback flow. We'll help instrument a webhook to your human-in-the-loop queue.
00:06:43 Priya: Great. Pricing — we need a ballpark so product can sign-off.
:00:06:47 Laura: I'll send a pilot pricing sheet; for bench runs we usually bill a fixed bench fee plus metered tokens. For a two-week pilot with your volume projected, I'll propose an estimate in the follow-up.
00:06:56 Mark: Security questionnaire — we'll share our vendor security questionnaire. You mentioned SOC2 + encryption — any additional compliance docs we should expect?
00:07:03 Laura: We'll attach SOC2 report, penetration test summary, and the architecture whitepaper. For KMS we'll add the integration checklist.
00:07:11 Ellen: Operationally, who runs the bench? Redwood or LumaHealth?
00:07:15 Diego: We'll run the bench in partnership. We'll upload the harness, but you'll need to provision the test environment and VPC endpoint. We'll coordinate times and run with your SRE on the control plane.
00:07:26 Priya: OK. Can we agree on the exact bench windows now? Week of July 6th for benching.
00:07:31 Ellen: Works for us. We'll reserve July 7-8 for nominal and peak runs.
00:07:35 Laura: Noted. Any other blockers?
00:07:38 Mark: Need to double-check legal for data processing addendum but that's routine. Also I want a clause that Redwood will never surface raw PII in support logs.
00:07:47 Laura: We'll include explicit commitments in the DPA and pilot agreement.
00:07:51 Priya: Quick note on acceptance: define pass/fail thresholds for quality and redaction. If we fail, is there a remediation period?
00:07:58 Laura: Standard pilot includes a 2-week remediation window to tune prompts, apply stricter redaction, or adjust batching. If remediation fails we move to a joint review call.
00:08:08 Diego: One technical nuance — quantization and model variant choice can affect hallucination rates and latency. We'll recommend two model variants for the bench: a lower-latency trimmed variant and a higher-quality one; we'll measure both.
00:08:20 Priya: Good idea. We'll include both in the acceptance matrix.
00:08:24 Laura: I'll capture responsibilities and next steps in the follow-up.
00:08:28 Priya: Thanks everyone.

(Transcript includes occasional mis-transcriptions: "KV" heard as "kay-v" in one spot, and "Key Vault" sometimes transcribed as "KeyVolt". Some filler: "uh", "mm-hmm" omitted for readability.)

Recap (live):
- Acceptance criteria: latency targets, quality thresholds, zero unredacted PII in persisted logs, cost target to be confirmed.
- Bench plan: warm up + nominal and peak runs (July 7-8), with synthetic PII test cases.
- Data handling: ephemeral by default, redaction rules for persisted review logs, Azure Key Vault integration for encrypted storage, per-route retention set to 7d ephemeral / 30d encrypted for review routes.
- Next steps: exchange redaction regex, Laura to send pricing and security docs, Diego to upload harness, Mark/Ellen to provision VPC endpoint and test credentials.

End of meeting.
